The Wise Woman of Abel
the wise WOOM-an of AY-bel
proper noun
From Hebrew Abel, the city Abel of Beth-maachah, where a wise woman treated with Joab and delivered the city.

See also: The Wise Woman of Abel

📖 Biblical Definition

The wise woman of Abel of Beth-maachah is unnamed in Scripture, yet honoured for her wisdom in delivering her city from destruction. When Sheba the son of Bichri, fleeing his failed revolt against David, had taken refuge in Abel, Joab and his host besieged the city and cast up a mount against the wall, battering to throw it down (2Sa 20:14–15). Then a wise woman cried from the city, asking to speak with Joab, and reasoned with him: “I am one of them that are peaceable and faithful in Israel: thou seekest to destroy a city and a mother in Israel: why wilt thou swallow up the inheritance of the LORD?” (2Sa 20:19). Joab answered that he sought not to destroy, but only the rebel Sheba; deliver him, and he would depart. The woman replied that Sheba’s head should be thrown over the wall; and she went to all the people in her wisdom, and they cut off the head of Sheba and cast it out to Joab, who blew the trumpet of retreat and withdrew (2Sa 20:21–22). By her counsel a whole city was spared, and a rebel’s revolt undone. She stands as a witness that the LORD has set His wisdom even in the unnamed and the lowly, and that one faithful soul, pleading for the inheritance of the LORD and for peace, may turn away wrath and save a multitude alive.

📜 Webster 1828 Definition

An unnamed wise woman of Abel of Beth-maachah who treated with Joab and saved her city by delivering up Sheba’s head.

expand to see more

THE WISE WOMAN OF ABEL, an unnamed woman of Abel of Beth-maachah (2Sa 20:16).

She cried to Joab as he besieged the city for Sheba’s sake.

She pleaded for “a city and a mother in Israel” (2Sa 20:19).

By her counsel the people cut off Sheba’s head (2Sa 20:22).

She thus saved the whole city from destruction.

📖 Key Scripture

2Sa 20:16 — "Then cried a wise woman out of the city, Hear, hear; say, I pray you, unto Joab, Come near hither, that I may speak with thee."

2Sa 20:19 — "I am one of them that are peaceable and faithful in Israel: thou seekest to destroy a city and a mother in Israel: why wilt thou swallow up the inheritance of the LORD?"

2Sa 20:21 — "The matter is not so: but a man of mount Ephraim, Sheba the son of Bichri by name, hath lifted up his hand against the king, even against David: deliver him only, and I will depart from the city. And the woman said unto Joab, Behold, his head shall be thrown to thee over the wall."

2Sa 20:22 — "Then the woman went unto all the people in her wisdom. And they cut off the head of Sheba the son of Bichri, and cast it out to Joab. And he blew a trumpet, and they retired from the city, every man to his tent. And Joab returned to Jerusalem unto the king."

⚠️ Modern Corruption

A figure of Scripture, not a contested doctrine; she witnesses that the LORD sets His wisdom in the lowly to turn away wrath and save a multitude.

expand to see more

This entry faces no significant postmodern redefinition. The principle to recover is that the LORD has set His wisdom even in the unnamed and the lowly, and that one faithful soul may turn away wrath and save a multitude. The wise woman of Abel did not lead an army nor hold an office; she reasoned with Joab from the wall, pleaded for the inheritance of the LORD, and by her counsel persuaded a whole city to deliver up the rebel and live. Wisdom and faithfulness, not station, made her a deliverer.

Her plea, “Why wilt thou swallow up the inheritance of the LORD?”, teaches a love for the peace and preservation of God’s people that puts away the one troubler for the good of the many. She did not shield the rebel Sheba; she gave him up, that the city of God’s inheritance might stand. So the dictionary marks her as a figure of the peaceable and faithful in Israel, whose wisdom prizes the good of the whole covenant people above the cause of the one who has lifted his hand against the king.

🔗 Greek & Hebrew Roots

Named from the city Abel of Beth-maachah, where an unnamed wise woman delivered the city.

expand to see more

Abel — the city Abel of Beth-maachah, in the far north of Israel.

A wise woman of the city cried to Joab from the wall.

She pleaded for a city and a mother in Israel.

By her wisdom the people gave up Sheba’s head.

She saved the whole city from destruction.

Usage

"Like the wise woman of Abel, one faithful soul may turn away wrath and save a multitude."

"She teaches that the LORD sets His wisdom in the lowly, that wisdom and faithfulness, not station, deliver."

"Her plea prizes the peace of God’s people above the cause of the one who lifts his hand against the king."
